title: Deeper/broader independent DXF projection, proprietary DWG route, and test-oracle trust
scope: Screen for a new independent DXF renderer or DWG/ACIS implementation route
Assess whether newly found peer test practices can cheaply strengthen existing semantic comparisons
Check whether the peer ASCII precision report implies a new local gap

method.kind: Read-only review of primary project documentation, repository metadata, and the current local plan
method.limitations: GitHub documentation and the package manifest are mutable project sources. No peer build, independent output comparison, corpus audit, renderer execution, DWG parse, kernel conversion, or native CAD acceptance was performed.

sources.revision: Mutable master README, package manifest, and test guide reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: The project describes an MPL-2.0 JavaScript 2D DXF viewer and test methods including canonical scene dumps, small generated DXF vectors, metamorphic checks, validator-negative checks, and an optional private corpus hash index. Its documentation lists incomplete DXF behavior, and states SVG debug output uses the same scene/reader path. These claims were not independently exercised.

The project documents a separately licensed, closed-source DWG parser. Its own scope note describes partial SAB decoding and best-effort wireframe or bounding-box fallback rather than full B-rep tessellation. It is not admitted as open-source implementation evidence or independent ACIS semantic evidence.

sources.revision: Public issue and linked pull request reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: The peer report concerns precision loss from ASCII floating-point formatting. The local plan already records the corresponding max_digits10 fix and exact binary64 controls as implemented under PAR-43/7Y.2a, so this is corroboration rather than a new local finding.

planDelta: Treat dxf-viewer only as a trigger-only optional 2D projection/render diagnostic; do not use it as a complete parser, writer-acceptance, DWG, or 3D oracle.
Exclude the proprietary mlightcad parser from open-source peer evidence and do not install it for this plan.
When an existing comparison validator is next touched, include one adjacent negative control proving that it detects a deliberately corrupted expected result.
Keep private corpus sweeps optional and composed-checkpoint-only; add no peer dependency, fixture, test registration, or per-slice full-suite/native validation.
workingTree: The repository worktree is broadly modified. This research added only the plan section/summary and this receipt; no staging or commit was attempted, and unrelated working-tree changes were preserved.
